page.text:
While pairing constructs sets of size two, the Axiom of Union enables the
consolidation of arbitrarily many sets. Given a set $X$ whose elements
are themselves sets, the union $\bigcup X$ collects every element
belonging to at least one member of $X$. In effect, the union axiom
flattens nested set structures by one level of containment.
